ARC-AGI-2 launch frontier models score humans
"LLMs Still Can't Plan; Can LRMs?" PlanBench o1 Mystery Blocksworld arxiv

sources_considered.why: Controlled three-party Turing test showing a big jump in mimicry.
Reports ARC-AGI-2 results with a human baseline at launch, a week before the post.
Planning evaluation of LLMs and o1 on PlanBench.

receipt.public_excerpt: When prompted to adopt a humanlike persona, GPT-4.5 was judged to be the human 73% of the time: significantly more often than interrogators selected the real human participant.

evidence_items.explanation: A pre-registered three-party Turing test found GPT-4.5 judged human more often than real humans. That shows great progress in human mimicry.

receipt.public_excerpt: The Arc Prize Foundation had over 400 people take ARC-AGI-2 to establish a human baseline. On average, “panels” of these people got 60% of the test’s questions right — much better than any of the models’ scores.

evidence_items.explanation: At launch, a week before the post, frontier models scored about 1-4% on a novel reasoning test where human panels got 60%. That is a large reasoning gap.

receipt.public_excerpt: As we shall see, while o1's performance is a quantum improvement on the benchmark, outpacing the competition, it is still far from saturating it.

evidence_items.explanation: The best reasoning model of late 2024 was still far from solving a standard planning benchmark. That fits the claim's planning gap, though the paper also notes big gains.

receipt.public_excerpt: ARC-AGI-1 was unbeaten for roughly five years until December 2024, when OpenAI released its advanced reasoning model, o3, which outperformed all other AI models and matched human performance on the evaluation.

evidence_items.explanation: Some reasoning tests had been matched at human level by late 2024. That cuts against the claim's degree, though not against its core.

unresolved_gaps: No dedicated common-sense benchmark with a human baseline was cited; the common-sense part rests on the general reasoning evidence.
'A lot still missing' has no threshold, so how big the gap is remains a matter of degree.
